title: Growing One's AI Tools: A Paradigm of Practice-Grown Tools
abstract: arXiv:2611.06132v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Professionals have long used software built for them by others. This article reports the growth of a professional computer-assisted interpreting (CAI) tool built by its own user, a conference interpreter without programming training. Drawing on an eight-week version-controlled record with telemetry from 133 logged sessions and over 20,000 recognized utterances, the article traces how real conference work drove the tool through 62 commits and six versions. The record shows capabilities deployed on the day their need appeared and one strategy change that cut median end-to-end delay by over a third within one afternoon. translated_title: 培育自己的AI工具：实践生长型工具的范式
translated_abstract: 长期以来，专业人士使用的都是他人为其构建的软件。本文报告了由用户本人培育的专业计算机辅助口译（CAI）工具的成长历程，该用户是一位未经编程训练的会议口译员。基于为期八周的版本控制记录以及来自133个记录会话和超过20,000条识别语句的遥测数据，本文追踪了真实的会议工作如何推动该工具经历62次提交和六个版本的发展。记录显示，新功能在其需求出现的当天即被部署，而一次策略调整在短短一个下午内将中位端到端延迟削减了超过三分之一。文章随后提出了“实践生长型工具”范式，其界定特征包括：从使用到培育的转变、工具与实践通过故障与修复实现的共同演化、有界本地计算，以及由此得出的评估推论，并提出了三个命题，以迈向将工具纳入考量的从业者评估。
tldr: 本文提出“实践生长型工具”新范式：一位无编程背景的会议口译员依据真实口译工作需求自行培育出计算机辅助口译工具，展现了工具与实践通过故障与修复共同演化的过程，并主张应将工具纳入对从业者的评估体系。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the paradigm of "practice-grown tools," demonstrating how a conference interpreter without programming training grew their own computer-assisted interpreting tool driven by real work needs, revealing tool-practice co-evolution through breakdown and repair, and advocating for tool-inclusive assessment of practitioners.
